opening.headline: Learn how to solve the hassle of re-posting the same material in each conversation and explaining the same background over and over again with projects and knowledge spaces.
body: I uploaded a product manual PDF and described my company on Monday, but when I open a new conversation on Wednesday, I have to start over with the same file and the same description from the beginning. The same goes for Friday. As more data becomes available, this repetition not only takes more time, but also increases the number of mistakes.

In this lesson, we'll explore the differences between one-off chats, where each conversation starts anew, and projects and knowledge spaces, which gather related materials and guidance in one place. After comparing the components of ChatGPT, Claude's project, and Gemini Notebook side by side, we follow the instructor's commentary on why the project is suitable for Q&A in the product manual.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the difference between chat and project/knowledge space
You can distinguish where to place repeatedly used material.

screens.outro: First, let's think about how much material you all write together.

screens.title: Think about frequently used materials
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. There are no fields to enter or submit, so think about it first and then click it.

visual.alt: Illustration of several file icons scattered next to a question card.

items.prompt: How many materials do you often use together when working with AI?
items.answer: In most cases, it's more than you think. Even if there are just three or four materials that you refer to every time, such as business regulations, product manuals, previous reports, and glossaries, uploading them for each conversation becomes a huge burden. This number is the first clue to determining whether you need space.

items.prompt: Are you uploading new data for each conversation?
items.answer: If so, it means you already have repeated input. Uploading the same file repeatedly is not something that should be done by humans; it is something that space should do for you.

items.prompt: Are you rewriting the same background information every time?
items.answer: Background explanations, answer rules, and tone of voice are also repeated contexts. These contents are not written down in the conversation, but are set as guidelines and apply to all conversations.

screens.outro: Now that we've summarized our experience, let's compare how a one-off chat differs from a project.

screens.title: Difference between one-time chat and project
screens.lead: Flip the switch to compare how material and context are handled in a one-time chat versus a project.

states.label: one-time chat
states.body:
Since each conversation starts anew, you need to add the necessary data and background at that time. This method is the easiest if you are writing the material once and finishing it. Because there is no setup required and you can get started right away.

However, in tasks that require the same data and explanations to be written repeatedly, the amount that must be entered each time accumulates. The previous Monday, Wednesday, and Friday cases are this case. Longer conversations can push the front end out of the context window, or the limit of how much the model can see at one time. If important data and rules are contained within a conversation, the moment you close that conversation, the next conversation will have to be recreated from scratch, and content may be missed in the process.

states.label: project
states.body:
The ChatGPT help explains that the project brings together related chats, files, and instructions in one place to keep them in sync. You can start work on one device and continue on another, and reuse projects for recurring tasks like weekly research or content drafting.

Claude Help describes a project as an independent workspace with its own chat history and knowledge base. Content posted to the knowledge base will be used in all chats for that project. However, the content is not automatically shared between chats within the project, and must be added to knowledge to be shared.

screens.outro: Let's take a look at the picture to see what components are in the project.

screens.title: Components of a project: instructions and knowledge files
screens.lead: You can see what each area of the project screen does by selecting the numbered marker in the picture. Please select them in order starting from number 1.

visual.alt: Instructions area, knowledge file area, chat list, and share button are arranged on the project screen.
labels: Answer in a polite tone and tell me the page number of the manual.

markers.label: Project Guidelines
markers.title: Where you decide how to behave
markers.body: Write down how the model will behave and respond in conversations within the project. An example of a ChatGPT tip is "Act like my marketing mentor. Be concise, in bullet points, and ask questions back." These guidelines apply only within that project and take precedence over global custom guidelines. In Claude, when you save project instructions, they will be used in all chats for that project.

markers.label: knowledge file
markers.title: A place to post reference information
markers.body: This is where reference materials are posted. ChatGPT allows you to upload PDFs, spreadsheets, documents, images, or paste text; the number of files varies depending on your plan. Claude uploads documents, text files, and code snippets to his knowledge base. On paid plans, when knowledge approaches the limit of how much a model can view at once, RAG mode is automatically turned on, increasing capacity by up to 10x. RAG is a method of finding and using parts related to a question from a large number of materials.

markers.label: chat
markers.title: A place for questions only
markers.body: This is a conversation that starts within a project. The guidance and knowledge is already there, so all you have to do is add this question to your conversation. You can create multiple chats within a project, but according to Claude's help, content between chats is not shared unless you add it to the knowledge.

markers.label: share
markers.title: How to write with a team
markers.body: Claude's Team and Enterprise plans allow you to make projects private or public to your organization, with separate viewing and editing permissions. Even in public projects, your chats remain private. The scope of sharing features varies depending on your plan and administrator settings.

data.notes: Google informs us that Gemini Notebook is the same independent product renamed from NotebookLM. A notebook can contain up to 50 free user sources, each of up to 500,000 words or 200MB. Each notebook is independent from each other, so information from multiple notebooks is not retrieved and written at once.

screens.outro: Let’s solve the product manual Q&A case based on the comparison.

screens.title: Explanation: Why is product manual Q&A a project?
screens.lead: The instructor explains the customer support team's product manual questions and answers step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed.

steps.title: Check the situation
steps.body: Customer support team agents look at product manuals every day and answer customer questions. Now, every time I open a conversation, I upload the manual PDF and rewrite the answer rules. The same preparations are repeated several times a day.

steps.title: Step 1: Find repetition
steps.body: It picks out the same thing every time. The first is the product manual PDF. The second rule is “Answer in a polite tone and tell me the page number of the manual.” Conversely, what changes every time is the customer’s question.

steps.title: Step 2: Decide where to place it
steps.body: Manuals that are repetitive materials are uploaded to the knowledge file. Recurring rules are written in the project guidelines. Questions that change each time are included in the conversation. If you do this, the conversation will only contain questions.

steps.title: Step 3: Check results
steps.body: After creating a project, all an agent needs to do is open a new conversation and write a question. Manuals and rules are already in place. Even if the questions change, answers are answered using the same manual and the same rules, which increases the consistency of answers.

steps.title: Instructor's explanation
steps.body: There are three reasons why the project is right. This is because the same material is written over and over again, the rules are the same every time, and multiple conversations require the same context. Even if the material is only a single manual, the benefits of a project with a large number of iterations are clear.

screens.outro: Next, we will check for cases where team sharing and projects do not match.

screens.title: Commentary: When shared scope and space are not required
screens.lead: By selecting and expanding each item, you can see the instructor's commentary on cases where the project does not match the scope of team sharing.

items.title: Shared scope: When using with a team
items.body: When you create a project on Claude's Team and Enterprise plans, you can choose to make it private (only those you invite) or public (everyone in your organization can see and use it). If ten agents work with the same manual, it is appropriate to make the organization public or share it with designated members. Even in public projects, your chat content is not visible to others. If your administrator has turned off sharing, you will not be able to use this feature.

items.title: If the project doesn't fit
items.body: A one-time chat is sufficient for materials that will be written and completed once. For example, if you create a project to summarize meeting materials for today only, preparation will be more cumbersome. The effort of creating space is only valuable if it can be repaid over and over again.

items.title: If Gemini Notebook is not right for you
items.body: Gemini Notebook is a tool that answers questions based on sources uploaded to the notebook. Therefore, it is not suitable for general knowledge or creative work outside the source. Additionally, since each notebook is independent, questions across multiple notebooks are not processed at once. Source-based answers and citations are ideal for critical research.

items.title: Data volume and space capacity
items.body: As data increases, capacity becomes an issue. Claude's paid plan increases capacity in RAG mode when your project knowledge approaches its limit. Gemini Notebook has upper limits on the number and size of sources. If you have a lot of material to upload, you need to select only what you need and organize the sources.

items.title: Instructor's Evaluation Criteria
items.body: There are three ways to determine whether you need space: How many times do you use the same material over and over again? Should I share it with my team? How much data is there? The more repetition, the more sharing, and the more material, the more valuable the space becomes.

screens.outro: Lastly, I will summarize the contents of this class.

screens.title: The repetition context is placed in space.
screens.lead: The contents so far are organized as a criterion for determining where to place repetitive materials.

paragraphs: Repeated context is not included in each conversation, but is placed in a space. Projects are your instructions and knowledge files, and Gemini Notebooks are your sources, gathering recurring material and rules in one place. This leaves only this question in the conversation and eliminates the preparation.

The distinction is simple. Materials that are the same every time are placed in the knowledge file, rules that are the same every time are placed in the project guidelines, and questions that change every time are placed in the conversation. For materials that will be written and completed once, a one-time chat is sufficient.

The Monday, Wednesday, Friday repetition we saw initially is solved by putting the product manual and answer rules once on the project. However, since content is not automatically shared between chats within a project, results that need to be continued must be added to the knowledge. ChatGPT also allows you to save useful responses as project source for reuse in future chats. If I've posted the same material more than once in my line of work, that material is a good candidate for a space.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: Put the data in the knowledge file, the rules in the instructions, and this question in the conversation. Determine whether space is needed by number of repetitions, sharing needs, and amount of material.

glossary.def: Each conversation starts anew and material and background are added at a time.
A workspace that brings together relevant chat, instructions, and knowledge files in one place.
A description of the behavior that applies to all conversations within the project.
This is a resource that can be placed on a project or notebook for reference.
This is Google's notebook-type space where answers and output are created based on uploaded sources.

misconceptions.myth: Content is automatically shared between chats within a project.
misconceptions.fact: Claude Help explains that even within a project, only what you put into the knowledge base is shared across all chats. The results you need to keep writing about need to add to your knowledge.

misconceptions.myth: When you upload a file, even the rules of conduct are determined for you.
misconceptions.fact: Rules of conduct are placed in the instructions, and references are placed in the file. The two roles are different and must be prepared together.

misconceptions.myth: It's always good to create space.
misconceptions.fact: For materials that will be written and completed once, a one-time chat is convenient. You can recoup your efforts by using space over and over again.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Repeated context is not included in each conversation, but is placed in a space.
Projects are organized around instructions and knowledge files, and Gemini Notebooks are organized around sources.
Every time, the same material is placed in the knowledge file, the same rules are placed in the instructions, and questions that change are placed in the conversation.
Determine whether space is needed by number of repetitions, sharing needs, and amount of material.
